text:
Aflatoxin contamination, caused by the fungus Aspergillus flavus.

Symptoms: an olive-green to black powdery mould can appear on kernels, especially at the kernel tip or at wound sites, under warm, humid storage conditions or when grain has been exposed to prolonged wet conditions in the field before harvest. Critically, aflatoxin contamination is not always visible -- grain can be contaminated with the toxin without obvious surface mould.

Management: because aflatoxin is highly toxic to humans and animals and cannot be removed once grain is contaminated, prevention is essential. Key practices: harvest promptly at physiological maturity rather than leaving mature grain in wet field conditions; dry grain quickly to a safe moisture content after harvest (see the grain drying topic); and store dried grain in dry, well-ventilated conditions to prevent mould growth during storage. Any visibly mouldy grain should not be used for human or animal consumption, since visible mould is a strong warning sign even though its absence doesn't guarantee safety.
